name: forgiving-params-session
details: Implement forgiving parameter naming for str_replace command in both unified and one-tool-per-command modes. Accept both old_str/new_str AND old_string/new_string with proper validation.

tasks.name: Update Zod Schemas
tasks.details:
Update schemas in mcp-server.ts for both modes:
1. MemoryCommandSchema str_replace variant (unified mode)
2. StrReplaceCommandSchema (one-tool-per-command mode)

Make old_str, old_string, new_str, new_string all optional, add refine validation for:
- At least one old_* variant provided
- At least one new_* variant provided
- NOT both old_str and old_string
- NOT both new_str and new_string

tasks.name: Update TypeScript Interface
tasks.details: Update StrReplaceCommand interface in operations.ts to support both naming conventions with optional fields

tasks.name: Update str_replace Function
tasks.details:
Add normalization logic at the start of str_replace function to:
1. Determine which old_* variant was provided
2. Determine which new_* variant was provided
3. Use normalized values throughout the function
4. Update logging to show which variants were used

tasks.name: Write Comprehensive Tests
tasks.details:
Add tests for all forgiving parameter scenarios:
1. old_str + new_str (original)
2. old_string + new_string (alternative)
3. Mixed: old_str + new_string
4. Mixed: old_string + new_str
5. Conflict detection: old_str + old_string (should fail)
6. Conflict detection: new_str + new_string (should fail)
7. Missing both variants (should fail)

tasks.name: Manual Testing with MCP-Debug
tasks.details:
Test with actual MCP-Debug tool:
1. Test unified tool mode with both naming conventions
2. Test one-tool-per-command mode with both naming conventions
3. Verify error messages for conflicts are clear
4. Request server reconnect from user
